response.outputText: {"title":"Lockout and Tagout: Maintaining Isolation","question":"When several workers are all involved in isolating the same piece of equipment, what is the correct procedure for controlling re-energisation?","answers":[{"text":"Each worker applies their own lock to a multi-lock hasp, and the equipment cannot be re-energised until every lock, including the last one, is removed.","correct":true,"feedback":"Correct. When several workers are involved, each applies their own lock to a multi-lock hasp so the equipment cannot be re-energised until the last lock is removed."},{"text":"One worker applies a single lock on behalf of the whole group, and any group member can remove it once their task is finished.","correct":false,"feedback":"This is incorrect because only the worker who applied a lock may remove it, and each worker involved must apply their own lock rather than relying on one shared lock."},{"text":"Each worker attaches a warning tag without a lock, since the tag alone is enough to prevent the equipment from being re-energised.","correct":false,"feedback":"This is incorrect because a tag without a lock is only a warning, not a control, and must never be used alone where a lock can be fitted."},{"text":"Workers take turns locking and unlocking the equipment as they finish their individual tasks, so the equipment can be re-energised as soon as the first person leaves.","correct":false,"feedback":"This is incorrect because the equipment cannot be re-energised until all locks, including the last one, are removed, not just the first worker's lock."}],"evidenceIds":["ev-s15","ev-s20","ev-s21","ev-s22","ev-s23","ev-s24","ev-s25"]}
